a) How this affects the patient: The patient requires regular heart check-ups to monitor potential heart conditions.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Approximately 38% of individuals with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to heart valves, holes in heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences feeding difficulties, is extremely picky with food textures, and struggles to consume meals.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Feeding difficulties are common in individuals with KBG syndrome, with some requiring short-term nasogastric tube feeding.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences hypotonia, characterized by weak muscles and impaired movement and balance. Additionally, there are speech delays and difficulty understanding others, indicating neurological concerns.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of individuals with KBG syndrome experience seizures, which typically respond to anti-epileptic treatment.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has experienced otitis media or glue ear, leading to conductive hearing loss and seeking regular ear checks.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many individuals with KBG syndrome have experienced otitis media or glue ear, which can lead to conductive hearing loss and require periodic ear checks.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has mentioned struggling with speech clarity and difficulty making oneself understood, suggesting possible vision or speech-related issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome may exhibit various ocular conditions, including astigmatism and short- or long-sightedness, which could impact their vision and communication abilities.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences tooth chipping and breaking, necessitating frequent dental visits for protection and repair.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Teeth can be prone to chipping and breaking, requiring consistent care and monitoring by dentists.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has speech delays and difficulty expressing himself, impacting his academic performance and social interactions.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome often require additional support in school, with some needing EHCP and others benefiting from specialized settings.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient exhibits developmental delays, struggles with speech clarity, and has difficulty understanding others, affecting his overall behavioral and developmental trajectory.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome may experience various behavioral differences, including autism spectrum disorder (ASD), ADHD, or anxiety, which can influence their behavior and social interactions.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has an unusual structure of his spinal bones, which can lead to scoliosis, and delayed fontanelle closure‚ adding to his health concerns.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of individuals with KBG syndrome have an increased curvature of the spine (scoliosis), and delayed fontanelle closure‚ which are additional skeletal concerns.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
a) How this affects the patient: The patient needs regular heart check-ups, dental visits, and monitoring for hypotonia and speech delays.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome may require ongoing monitoring for heart conditions, hormonal imbalances, palatal abnormalities, and tethered cord conditions, among others.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a heart valve abnormality that requires regular monitoring.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient can be picky with food and will refuse to eat certain things, indicating potential feeding difficulties.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences seizures, which are managed by doctors but still occur periodically.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, which typically respond to anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a degree of hearing loss and speech delay, with occasional requests for repetition of what was said.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many individuals with KBG syndrome have speech delay and subtle palatal abnormalities, which may impact their communication abilities.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has scoliosis, which affects his posture and possibly impacts his overall mobility and activity level.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism and myopia, which may require corrective measures.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences tooth sensitivity and frequent visits to the dentist for various dental issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Dental concerns are common in KBG syndrome, including weak enamel and need for frequent dental procedures such as grommet insertions and tooth fillings.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has varying levels of educational attainment, with some obtaining qualifications and others needing support in mainstream settings.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, but some children with smaller ANKRD11 deletions may have more significant limitations.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient exhibits developmental delays and behavioral differences, including speech delay and subtle palatal abnormalities.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome often have developmental delay and various behavioral differences, such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD), ADHD, or anxiety.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has an unusual structure of his spinal bones, which can lead to scoliosis and potentially affect his posture and movement.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome may experience delayed closure of the soft spot on their head (anterior fontanelle), and a small number may have hip dysplasia, which can cause discomfort and functional issues.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
a) Recommendations for screening:
   - Regular dental check-ups
   - Hearing reviews at age 5
   - Palate review (especially if there are feeding difficulties or speech concerns)

b) Recommendations for treatments:
   - Management of seizures
   - Monitoring of heart valve abnormality
   - Correction of scoliosis
   - Management of tethered cord
   - Monitoring of hip dysplasia

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences rapid breathing during intense play, which may indicate a potential cardiac issue.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences rapid breathing during intense play, suggesting possible cardiac issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has slow weight gain compared to peers, despite a balanced diet.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences seizures, which are managed with medication and monitored by neurologists.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, which typically respond to anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient turns the volume of the TV very high, indicating possible ear-related issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many children with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties and some require treatment for otitis media or glue ear.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has myopia, which affects her vision and requires correction.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism and short- or long sightedness.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient needs regular dental check-ups to maintain tooth health.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Feeding difficulties and lack of interest in feeding can be significant and long-lasting in some individuals with KBG syndrome.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has varying levels of educational attainment, with some obtaining qualifications and others needing support in mainstream settings.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, but there is a wide range of eventual ability, with some children acquiring mobility and other skills around the same age as “typical” children and others showing more obvious delay.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has noticeable differences in posture when standing or walking, which may indicate underlying neurological or muscular issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioral differences such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD), ADHD, or anxiety, which may impact their daily life.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has scoliosis, which affects her spinal alignment.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Babies with KBG syndrome may experience delayed closure of the soft spot on their head (anterior fontanelle), and some children with KBG syndrome have an increased curvature of the spine (scoliosis).

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
a) Recommendations for screening:
   - Regular dental check-ups
   - Regular hearing reviews to age 5
   - Eyesight (ophthalmology) review
   - Check position of testes in boys
   
b) Recommendations for treatments:
   - Manage seizures with medication and monitor episodes
   - Work with neurologists to manage seizures
   - Ensure proper dental care
   - Address any associated palatal abnormalities
   - Monitor growth velocity and consider endocrine investigations
   - Manage scoliosis with physical therapy and possibly surgery if conservative treatments fail
   - Monitor posture and spinal alignment
   - Consider behavioral therapy and neurological assessments
